newsitem.title: USA: Sun Healthcare to expand Albuquerque HQ.
newsitem.headline: Sun Healthcare to expand Albuquerque HQ.

text.p: Sun Healthcare Group Inc plans to add 1,000 jobs at its Albuquerque headquarters after the city agreed to issue $65 million in industrial revenue bonds for the expansion project, Chief Executive Andrew Turner said.

"The $65 million, two-building project will result in the addition of approximately 1,000 jobs within three years of the completion of the project, and will significantly expand Sun's international headquarters," Turner said in a statement.
He said the company plans to complete the project by 2004.
The Albuquerque City Council unanimously agreed in a meeting late Monday night to issue the bonds on behalf of Sun Healthcare, councillor Sam Bregman said.

Deirdre Firth, vice president of Albuquerque Economic Development Inc., said Sun Healthcare is responsible for the financing of the bonds and would receive tax breaks of around $16 million while the bonds are oustanding.
She said the expansion project would bring in about $116 million in net additional revenues for the city and state governments.
Sun Healthcare currently employs 350 people in Albuquerque and about 35,000 worldwide.
